title: Sensitivity at a right angle
statement: Let $n\ge 0$ and let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable. The rotation sensitivity of $A$ at angle $\pi/2$ is $2\gamma_n(A)\bigl(1-\gamma_n(A)\bigr)$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. If $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is measurable and $\alpha=\gamma_n(A)$, then $s_A(\pi/2)=2\alpha(1-\alpha)$.
